as_told.title: Documentary clip: binary model explains celestial observations

plain: A documentary called The Great Year proposes that our sun has a binary companion, a partner star it circles with. In this view, that slow dance explains the "great year," a long cycle in which the sky gradually shifts. The researcher Matt LaCroix describes the film's idea and notes that some thought the companion was the star Sirius. Clips from the documentary's own narrator also play on the episode, saying "the binary model confirms all of our celestial observations without the need for excessive torque or epicycle type explanations," meaning it avoids complicated workarounds. If true, it would change how the ancient sky cycles are explained.
